"""Core task operations. due_at throughout this module is in SECONDS, matching models.Task."""
import re
import time

from tinytasks.models import Task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all, next_id, save_all


EMAIL_RE = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)*\.[A-Za-z]{2,}")


def create_task(title: str, due_in_seconds: float) -> Task:
    """Create a task due `due_in_seconds` seconds from now. Emails in the title are redacted."""
    title = EMAIL_RE.sub("[email]", title)
    tasks = load_all()
    task = Task(id=next_id(tasks), title=title, due_at=time.time() + due_in_seconds)
    tasks.append(task)
    save_all(tasks)
    return task


def get_overdue_tasks(now: float | None = None) -> list[Task]:
    """Tasks whose due_at (seconds) has already passed."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    return [t for t in load_all() if t.due_at < now]


def test_export_omits_archived_tasks(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("keep", due_in_seconds=60)
    gone = create_task("old", due_in_seconds=60)
    archive_task(gone.id)
    assert [d["title"] for d in export_tasks()] == ["keep"]


def test_add_redacts_email_in_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("call bob.smith@example.com and a@b.org today", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert t.title == "call [email] and [email] today"
    assert load_all()[0].title == "call [email] and [email] today"


def test_reschedule_rejects_past_due_date(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("stay", due_in_seconds=600)
    original = load_all()[0].due_at

**Compliance conflict:** Plexus memory had a rule from builder-1 (C2) that replaces emails in titles with `[email]`. It comes from the compliance memo, which is still marked DRAFT v0.3. This change reverses that rule, so compliance should confirm before it ships. I recorded the new behavior in Plexus, which replaced the old C2 fact, and noted that it needs sign-off.
